intake_questions.who_may_book: The owner, a manager or the office manager of the business that is cleaned, or the property manager of the building. A tenant who doesn't control a shared area needs the property manager's OK for it.

stop: biohazards: blood, body fluids, needles, a crime or trauma scene
a mold patch over the state's size cutoff
floors, stairs or ladders that aren't safe
safety_and_stop_words.go_on: Yes, with the area left out (sewage, biohazards, a spill, mold, wiring, a floor). No, for a gas smell, smoke or fire. Pest problems wait for pest control.
stop_action: A gas smell, smoke or fire: leave and call 911. Rosie never places the call. No booking until it's safe.

Sewage, biohazards, an unknown spill, asbestos or lead dust, or mold over the cutoff: Rosie says a cleaner can't take that on and points to a specialist. The rest of the space can still be booked with that area left out.
Sewage: keep people out of the area, and stay out if the water is near outlets.
Sparking or exposed wiring, or an unsafe floor: stay out of the area; no booking for it until it's fixed.
Bedbugs or rodents: pest control comes first; the clean is booked after.
Home cleaning isn't this business: no booking, and the AI can look for a home cleaning company.

staff.licenses_or_certificates: None per person unless the state's form says so.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs quotes over the limit. The office manager may too; the owner's answer wins.
staff.crews: Two per site: a lead, who holds the entry code and texts DONE, and a helper. A person who works alone at a site adds an emergency contact, and a missed safety check gives that contact the job's address only.

children_and_age.who_may_book: The owner, a manager or the office manager of the business that is cleaned, or the property manager of the building. A tenant who doesn't control a shared area needs the property manager's OK for it.

visit.check_in: Someone there: the code at the door, entered by the crew lead. Nobody there (most plan visits): no code; the lead opens the door with the key, fob or code the business gave.
visit.done: Before photos of each area, an area-by-area checklist, after photos from the same angles. DONE with after photos when nobody's there. Photos never show screens, papers, people or private offices.
visit.changes_at_visit: Add-ons only when the on-site contact asks, priced before they're done. A large space clean is priced before any work. A right to cancel only where the state's rules give one.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Usually none for office cleaning and floor care. Where the state's or city's rules require a business license or registration for janitorial work, the form asks for it. Work at height (outside windows above the ground floor), pest control, mold, asbestos and biohazard cleanup are separate licensed or certified trades in some places and are not offered here.
license.who: The business. Crew members need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
license.ask: The company's business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one.
license.insurance: General liability, workers' comp and a janitorial bond are common, and a building often asks for a certificate of insurance. 'Insured' or 'bonded' is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: Crew members who hold keys or codes: the business's own word that they are checked, or a check Rosie holds where the state's rules require one. It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.

never_in_a_text: Entry, fob, lockbox, door, garage and alarm codes
Health reasons, like an allergy behind a product to avoid
languages: English and Spanish. The crew's language shows on the job.
